pr_title: Fix Garmin Connect integration with python-garminconnect-aio
pr_body:
Garmin and/or Cloudflare changed behavior of API this patch (medium update) fixes the issue.

I replaced python-garminconnect with python-garminconnect-aio
https://github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect-aio/
An async version of the original one without scraping code.
Optimized integration code along the way.

@frenck Is this too late for Release 2021.5.5 ?
It fixes a broken garmin_connect integration (in use by 613 users) ;-)

The python-garminconnect module simply has a single equests.session() call replaced by a cloudscraper.Cloudscraper call.

https://github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect/commit/f9fda0120db40446d55ba9e4498a8c210b5824e4#diff-49c607e2f2c65952b7d8e18fefba6af12a22119f68f236d35066a6f6ad2f8964

https://github.com/VeNoMouS/cloudscraper/blob/master/cloudscraper/__init__.py#L117

Is this the use case the webscraping.md document wants to prevent?

I mean in a sense every request code does some kind of 'webscraping' to get data (tokens etc) from http calls.
This will run on any request when it happens (not just authentication of Garmin), next it will scrape/parse HTML & JavaScript to bypass CloudFlare's Anti-bot.

It's seems the only way to query the API behind the Cloudflare service reliably.

I will try to get it working without the Cloudscraper module with some other code tomorrow, but if this doesn't work stable I guess we need to remove the Garmin Connect integration from core and it will show up in HACS, so nothing is gained, since the same code is running inside the HA installations of 600+ users.

We cannot get/use the official API unless we pay 1K $ and be screened as a respectable developer and I guess open-source is a no-no since this gives away the API details for everyone.

I have contacted Garmin about this nevertheless, maybe they look at it differently now.

> It's seems the only way to query the API behind the Cloudflare service reliably.

I, personally, don't agree on the reliable part. Deliberately bypassing a technique that was developed to prevent what the package does, is (in the end) a cat & mouse game.

The web scraping ADR is partly in place to prevent that game.

@MartinHjelmare, can I have a second opinion on that?
I agree with @frenck that the cloudscraper usage falls under the not allowed web scraping we've defined in ADR 4.
Thanks for the input, back to the drawing board... (and a bottle of whiskey)
I'm supporting you with a bottle of Bacardi Carta Negra ;-), @cyberjunky

I have created a minimal version of the older python-garminconnect package still only using the requests module and implementing only the methods needed for the garmin_connect integration.
Simplified a lot of stuff underneath.

It's called python-garminconnect-ha 
https://github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect-ha

Unfortunately, users need to remove and add the Garmin Connect integration and run the setup again.

@frenk @balloob BTW: I got a reply from Garmin on my email asking about possible access to the Garmin Connect API documentation, see below.
My guess is that we don't match all these rules, especially the last one.

---
In general, to get an access to API, you will need to be enterprise entity and provide following information during application process. 
 
• a valid website,
• a privacy policy link available for everybody on your homepage,
• a running business model or business plan, 
• no personal use

Our API is governed by license agreement that has to be signed by a person who is applying on behalf of their organization and Garmin. 
Are you able to legally represent 'Home Assistant'?
It seems some dev stuff got in, need to fix that, DONE
If the two libraries share most of the code, maybe it would be better to just have an option for the request instance? Otherwise the development of one package will not benefit the other package.

That would be ideal, but the full blown package is used by a lot of people for their own software projects, for example for downloading training data. 
They benefit greatly from the new cloudscraper module, which has no rate limit it seems, you can download as much as you can without hitting it, where as the requests package based code blocks your requests for **a whole hour** if you execute more than around 100 queries per hour. I will probably optimize the full blown version the same way i did with the HA version and only replace the requests with the cloudscraper package to keep them manageable.

EDIT: Ah, you mean select the package to use at runtime depending on the use case, would that be acceptable to include in home assistant?
Yes, if we're not doing web scraping we're not breaking ADR 4

I have thought about it, and decided to keep the minimal python-garminconnect-ha just for home assistant.
The full blown one has more development and I don't want to make things more complicated for future HA PR's
I have some things written down to fix (implement DataCoordinator, add missing unit_for_measurement's and add other sensors.
But will make a new PR for those later (like in a few weeks)

Please review this PR (I have changed the title) to be included in a next stable release update if possible. 2021.5.6 maybe?
Thanks!
Really, is waiting for a check here at HA always taking so long?
Thanks very very much, Cyberjunky, for all the hard work. You are a champ!
